one_line_contribution: Treat the noise of a counterfactual per-item memory-value estimate as the estimand rather than a nuisance: by repeated leave-one-out re-runs on fresh (game, seed) cells of a deliberately heterogeneous ALFWorld bank, measure how many retrievals a per-item rank needs, how much a top-ranked item's apparent excess shrinks when re-measured on disjoint games, and the retrieval count below which LOO-score pruning is indistinguishable from random pruning.
closest_prior_work: Two threats, one verified by ID and one only partly. (a) CUE-R (arXiv:2604.05467, verified via the literature command, S2, 2026-04-07) already does intervention-based per-evidence-item utility measurement (REMOVE/REPLACE) with an evidence-role taxonomy, and Source Attribution in RAG (arXiv:2507.04480, verified, ECML/PKDD workshop 2025) does document-level Shapley with an explicit budget-vs-fidelity analysis. Neither reports seed variance, a retrievals-to-reliability curve, or re-measurement of selected items, and both are single-shot RAG rather than multi-step agents, so they threaten the measurement apparatus but not the reliability claim. (b) The real mechanism threat is the data-valuation literature on rank stability under a stochastic utility: my S2 query returned 'Robust Data Valuation with Weighted Banzhaf Values' (NeurIPS 2023, 29 citations; the tool returned no arXiv id for it, so the ID is unverified), which parameterizes utility stochasticity ('Kronecker noise') and proves which semivalue keeps ranks most stable under it — i.e. the abstract question 'how noisy can the utility be before per-item ranks are meaningless' is settled work, and the underlying Data Banzhaf paper (Wang and Jia 2023) the proposal cites from memory was again not returned by either channel, so I could not verify it either. Data Shapley itself (arXiv:1904.02868, verified, ICML 2019, 1190 citations) is the standard the proposal correctly says reports no sample-size-to-reliability curve. What survives as new is narrow but real: variance components measured rather than assumed, on an LLM agent with a binary episode outcome, plus the downstream pruning-decision threshold. That is a domain instantiation of known statistics (generalizability theory, Spearman-Brown, regression to the mean, empirical-Bayes shrinkage), not a new mechanism, and the paper must be judged as a measurement report.
strongest_objection: Most of the proposal is one number, and that number is already implied by measurements the authors have in hand. P1's R(12), P2's shrinkage slope (which is algebraically R(6)), P3a's null, and P6a's own positive control are all monotone functions of var_item/var_within on the same 120-item panel; the proposal's 'shared terms' list concedes this. With the pilot's within-item SD of delta at 0.45, R(12) >= 0.5 requires a between-item SD of per-item LOO effect of about 13 net points, on a panel whose entire 3-item retrieved set is worth only +27 net over k=0 and +17.2 over static3, and whose one genuinely heterogeneous class (the 100 planted items) is excluded from the panel by construction. So the headline finding 'a per-item rank needs tens of retrievals' is settled by arithmetic on Step-0 numbers before the 35,300 episodes are spent, and the round's own binding rule forbids predictions entailed by the setup. Worse, the one deliverable that is not entailed - the pruning threshold n* in E5 - is a property of the authors' own contamination design, not of memory banks: the bottom-100 cut can only beat random to the extent it is enriched for the 100 planted wrong-procedure items, whose prevalence (100 planted against roughly 200 unfiltered self-written plus the expert set) and effect size (a procedural step replaced by a wrong action, i.e. maximally harmful) are both knobs the authors set. A reviewer will say the paper reports a threshold for detecting sabotage the authors inserted at a rate they chose, then names it 'the pruning threshold'. Secondary but nameable: P5a's 5-net and P6b's 4-net thresholds sit inside the cells' own stated CI half-widths (3.9 and 2.6), which violates the proposal's own pre-registered margin rule of half-width + 2 net with a 5-net minimum - an internal inconsistency in the Measurement section, not just a power complaint. And the panel is defined by selecting the 1,200 stream games so that 120 items each get >= 24 retrievals, i.e. the reliability curve is measured on the most-retrieved, most generic items, while the practically hard case - the long tail retrieved once or twice, where pruning decisions actually bite - is structurally excluded.
what_would_fix_it: 1) Make var_item and its class decomposition (expert vs self-written vs planted), with CIs, the reported estimand, and report R(n) as a derived curve; then the paper measures the heterogeneity of a real bank instead of predicting a low correlation that the noise floor guarantees. 2) Promote the predictions the entailment structure leaves open - P3b (score pruning at 24 retrievals beats random), P4 (LOO vs the zero-episode offline scorers), P5b (pair removal exceeds the sum of singles), P7 (static3 absorbs item-level credit) - to headline status, and demote P1/P2 to the calibration section they really are. 3) Turn n* into a curve rather than a point: run E5 at two planted prevalences (e.g. 100 and 30) or two planted severities, so the threshold is reported as a function of contamination rate and effect size and can be transported to a bank whose bad-item rate differs. 4) Cut the P6a terciles on a pooled high-n reader-A estimate or on item class, so the consumer-swap test does not inherit the low reliability P1 predicts. 5) Raise P5a to >= 8 net and P6b to >= 6 net, or add paired removals until the CI half-width is about 2 net, so both obey the proposal's own margin rule. 6) Report the reliability curve separately for the rarely-retrieved tail, or state explicitly that the result is conditional on items with >= 24 retrievals.
missing_baseline: E5 has S6, S24, R and O but no unpruned full-bank arm on the same U games, and no pruning arm driven by a zero-episode scorer. Both are demanded. Without the full-bank control you cannot tell whether removing 100 items helps, hurts, or does nothing on average, so S - R is a contrast between two interventions of unknown sign and cannot support a deployment recommendation; the round's binding rules already require a memory-matched arm. More damaging for the central claim: the offline DIG-style confidence-gain scorer (and a trivially cheap static procedure-consistency check against the type's procedure, which is what the planted items violate) is compared to LOO on detection AUC in P4 but never given its own pruning arm, even though it costs zero environment episodes. The paper's decision claim is 'you need about N retrievals per item before score pruning is worth it'; the only way that claim survives review is if 24 LOO retrievals per item beat the zero-retrieval offline scorer at the same pruning task, not just random. A reviewer will also ask for the provenance heuristic (prune all unfiltered self-written items) as a free baseline.
preprint_collision: No verified collision. My queries, all answered by channel (a), the literature command (Semantic Scholar + HF Papers, both channels reported ok); WebSearch was unavailable in this session and was not used. (1) mechanism, no recency filter: 'how many samples does a per-item leave-one-out value estimate need rank stability noisy utility' - nothing on point; nearest were Leave-one-out Distinguishability (arXiv:2309.17310, a privacy/memorization notion, not valuation noise) and Rank List Sensitivity of Recommender Systems (arXiv:2201.12686). (2) mechanism, --recent (last 12 months): 'counterfactual per-item value of retrieved memory items leave-one-out re-runs reliability LLM agent' - 9 hits, none per-item counterfactual; the closest were Memory Reward Inflation (arXiv:2608.00017, self-graded reward inflation, not counterfactual), A-MAC (arXiv:2603.04549, admission scores, no ground truth), MMA (arXiv:2602.16493, a reliability score that is never validated against an intervention). (3) closest named method: 'Data Banzhaf robust data valuation noisy utility rank stability sample complexity' - returned Robust Data Valuation with Weighted Banzhaf Values (NeurIPS 2023, S2, no arXiv id returned) and Robust Consensus in Ranking Data Analysis (arXiv:2303.12878), but again not the Data Banzhaf paper itself, confirming the proposal's honest report that this citation is from memory. (4) 'winner's curse selection bias regression to the mean top-ranked noisy estimates data selection shrinkage' - no pre-emption; only Compound Estimation for Binomials (arXiv:2512.25042, verified) and generic shrinkage/selective-inference work. (5) --recent 'how many rollouts per memory item before pruning beats random pruning experience bank agent' - empty of anything relevant (rollout-budget systems work only, e.g. arXiv:2603.24840). (6) home vocabulary, no agent/memory words: 'variance components split-half reliability generalizability theory number of observations needed stable per-unit effect estimate' - empty of any LLM-memory application. ID verification: I verified arXiv:1904.02868 (Data Shapley, ICML 2019), arXiv:2507.04480 (Source Attribution in RAG), arXiv:2604.05467 (CUE-R), arXiv:2512.25042 (Compound Estimation for Binomials), arXiv:2603.10960 (Scorio, titled 'Ranking Reasoning LLMs under Test-Time Scaling'), arXiv:2607.22002 (VIGOR), arXiv:2608.02508 (RoMeRL), arXiv:2606.24595 (MEMPROBE), arXiv:2602.01399 (OddSHAP) and arXiv:2512.10696 (ReMe); I did not verify arXiv:2607.22562 (SF-AMS) or the Data Banzhaf paper, and the latter is the one whose absence matters for the novelty argument. Judgement on the proposal's own check: it is above average for this program - five classed queries, the returns named with IDs, the failed Data Banzhaf retrieval reported honestly as a memory citation rather than papered over, and it correctly does not treat empty returns as proof. Two gaps: it never searched the vocabulary that actually owns the mechanism (generalizability theory / split-half reliability / variance components / Spearman-Brown, and the RL-side 'rollouts per unit to stabilize a per-item estimate'), which is where a scoop would most plausibly hide and where the brief's home-vocabulary rule points; and having failed twice to retrieve Data Banzhaf, it should have verified the closest semivalue-robustness result some other way, since that literature is the strongest threat to the 'rank stability under a stochastic utility' framing. My own runs of both vocabularies came back empty, so the check's conclusion stands, but it was luckier than it was thorough.
